To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) MEG data can provide estimates of brain structure, (2) these estimates can be made in terms of a distorted spherical manifold parameterisation, and (3) the functional assumptions which give rise to estimates of structure that are closer to empirical ground-truth also give rise to estimates that are closer the true structure.
We show how it is feasible to estimate brain structure from MEG.
it is possible to reconstruct plausible brain anatomy from MEG data.
